moduleNote: Player module — player concepts, skills, positions, condition/form/injury, actions. Excludes youth (separate module). Follows two player-facing rules: (1) no engine weights/formulas/coefficients/thresholds leaked, only qualitative priorities — BUT game-mechanics numbers that a player can verify by playing (match-type EXP multipliers, level cap, etc.) are fine to expose; (2) comparison and priority entries must cover ALL 10/9 skills — skipped skills must be explicitly bucketed into "almost no impact" with a reason, never silently omitted.

questions: what is the player composite rating
entries.answer:
PWI = Player Worth Index = the composite player rating. Higher number = stronger player.

In GoalXI, **PWI and overall are the same number** — the API returns both `pwi` and `overall` fields with identical values. `pwiDisplay` is the UI-rounded version for display.

PWI is driven by **three factors**:
- **Current skills (primary)** — higher values on the 10-skill panel → higher PWI
- **Potential (amplifier)** — same skills, a higher-potential player has a higher PWI ceiling
- **Form (fine-tune)** — good form nudges PWI up; bad form nudges it down

Higher PWI **doesn't guarantee better on-pitch performance** — position weight (where the player is lined up) and tactics also matter. Two players with the same PWI can perform very differently in different positions.

questions: what do the two radar lines mean
how to read a player growth ceiling
what is the dashed radar line
entries.answer:
Every player has two skill data sets:

- **currentSkills** (current, **solid** radar line) — the player's real ability right now; all PWI calculations use this
- **potentialSkills** (ceiling, **dashed** radar line) — the upper bound the player **can grow into**

The gap between the two = remaining growth headroom:
- **senior players**: usually very close together (mostly grown)
- **youth players**: large gap (still growing; specific drift is dynamic over time)

Skills basically stop rising once they hit potential. PWI reflects current ability, not potential directly.

> Youth reveal/promote mechanics live in the youth module (later).

questions: what do the 10 outfield skill panel items mean
what does each player skill affect
entries.answer:
Outfield players have a **10-skill** panel grouped into 4 dimensions:

**physical**
- **pace** — sprint speed, recovery runs, getting in behind
- **strength** — physical duels, headers, holding off opponents

**technical**
- **finishing** — goalscoring, shots in the box
- **passing** — through balls, long balls, crosses
- **dribbling** — 1v1 beat, take-on
- **defending** — tackles, interceptions, blocks

**mental**
- **positioning** — off-the-ball movement, defensive shape, runs into the box
- **composure** — calm finishing under pressure, no panic errors

**setPieces**
- **freeKicks** — direct free-kick taker quality
- **penalties** — penalty taker quality

Skill values range 0-20, default 10. Each skill's on-pitch contribution **varies by position** — see the per-position skill priority entries.

questions: what do GK reflexes handling aerial mean
why does GK have no finishing
entries.answer:
The GK skill panel has **9 items** (one fewer than outfield), grouped into 4 dimensions:

**physical** (same as outfield): pace, strength
**technical** (GK-specific, 3 items): reflexes, handling, aerial
**mental** (same as outfield): positioning, composure
**setPieces** (same as outfield): freeKicks, penalties

GKs don't get the outfield's finishing/passing/dribbling/defending (no point) — replaced by the 3 GK-specific technical skills.

**GKs are scored on a completely different formula than outfield** — the engine uses a dedicated GK calculation that focuses on **reflexes** and **handling**, with no position-weight influence. A high reflexes/handling radar means a good GK; pace/strength barely affect GK rating.

questions: how are physical technical mental setPieces grouped
entries.answer:
The 10/9 skills are grouped into 4 **functional dimensions** (purely UI organization; doesn't affect PWI math):

- **physical** — pace, strength
- **technical** — GK: reflexes/handling/aerial; outfield: finishing/passing/dribbling/defending
- **mental** — positioning, composure
- **setPieces** — freeKicks, penalties

The radar chart and skill list use these 4 groups for display. **The engine merges by position-weight, not by dimension.**

questions: difference between LOW REGULAR HIGH_PRO ELITE LEGEND
how to judge a player's potential tier
how to know if a player is worth training
entries.answer:
`potentialTier` is the **5-band potential label** for a player, with 5 color codes (weak → strong):

- **LOW** (grey) — low potential; maxes out as a bench / rotation option
- **REGULAR** (green) — first-team starter level; maxes out as a solid contributor, high cost/performance
- **HIGH_PRO** (gold) — high potential; maxes out as a top player, mid-table team core
- **ELITE** (pink) — elite; maxes out as a strong-team starter
- **LEGEND** (purple) — legendary; maxes out near the ceiling, rare (mostly from youth promotion or transfer wins)

> ⚠️ The tier label is assigned randomly by the generator and is **not directly equal to** the `potentialSkills` numbers. To judge "is this player worth training" look at the **gap between potentialSkills and currentSkills** more reliably (dashed vs solid radar).

Youth player tier labels are gated by `revealLevel` (fog-of-war) — you need to reveal enough skills to see them.

questions: full glossary of player position abbreviations
what do CD CDL CDR LB RB WBL WBR LM RM LW RW AM CM DM CFL CFR CF mean
entries.answer:
Full GoalXI position abbreviation reference (attack → defense order):

**Forward**
- `CF` center forward; `CFL`/`CFR` left/right center forward; `ST` center forward (alias)

**Winger (W)**
- `LW`/`RW` left/right winger (pure winger, plays in attack line)
- `LM`/`RM` actually maps to `WML`/`WMR` (wide midfielder, plays in midfield line — see W vs WM entry)

**Midfield (centralMidfield, CM)**
- `AM`/`AML`/`AMR` attacking midfielder (C/L/R); `CM`/`CML`/`CMR` central midfielder (C/L/R); `DM`/`DML`/`DMR` defensive midfielder (C/L/R)
- Aliases: `CAM`/`CDM`/`DMF`/`DMFL`/`DMFR` etc — historical names, engine folds automatically

**Defense (centerBack / fullback)**
- `CB`/`CBL`/`CBR` center back (C/L/R); `LB`/`RB` left/right back
- `WBL`/`WBR` wing back (L/R, more aggressive); `LWB`/`RWB` modern 1-slot wing back names
- Aliases: `CD`/`CDL`/`CDR` historical center-back names, engine folds to `CB`

**Goalkeeper**
- `GK` goalkeeper (single 1-slot)

**3-slot vs 1-slot**: `CBL`/`CB`/`CBR` are a 3-slot group (one `CB` family); `LW`/`LW1`/`LW2` are a 3-slot group too. The engine works on the family name; the specific slot is chosen in the formation editor.

**W (Winger, side attacker)** = `LW`/`RW` — **forward-line player**, sits high
- Main jobs: beat the fullback, cross, cut inside to shoot
- Position: furthest forward on each flank
- Engine focuses on **pace** and **dribbling** (these decide if a W is usable), with finishing as a bonus
- Operates mostly on their own flank; barely any central involvement

**WM (Wide Midfielder)** = `LM`/`RM` (engine actually uses `WML`/`WMR`) — **midfield-line player**, sits deeper
- Main jobs: midfield circulation, support the fullback, supply the winger
- Position: out wide on the midfield line
- Engine also looks at pace and dribbling, but **defending and positioning are required** (WMs must defend)

**Full 10-skill comparison**:
| Skill | Winger W (LW/RW) | Wide Midfielder WM (LM/RM) | Who's higher |
|---|---|---|---|
| **pace** | **Very high** | High | Winger |
| **strength** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **finishing** | Medium | Lower | Winger |
| **passing** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **dribbling** | **Very high** | High | Winger |
| **defending** | Very low | Medium | **Wide midfielder** |
| **positioning** | Lower | Medium | **Wide midfielder** |
| **composure** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **freeKicks** | - | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | - | Position-independent |

**Pattern**:
- **3 skills higher for W** (pace/dribbling/finishing) — attacking axis, W needs W-level body
- **2 skills higher for WM** (defending/positioning) — defensive/positioning axis, WM must defend
- **3 skills same** (passing/strength/composure) — common base for side players
- **2 skills position-independent** (freeKicks/penalties) — set-piece taker quality is personal

**One-liner**: **W is pure attack (almost no defending), WM is half-and-half (must track back)**. W goes up and doesn't come back; WM goes up and comes back.

**Practical tip**:
- Counter-attacking or needing a match-winner → W (LW/RW)
- Possession-based or needing wide circulation → WM (LM/RM)
- W cannot defend → must have an LM/RM or DM shielding behind (a WM covers both)

**LB/RB (Fullback)** — traditional side back, sits relatively deep
- Main jobs: contain the opposing winger, cover, **limited overlaps**
- Engine focuses on **defending and positioning** (defense-first), with low attacking weight
- Lateral push demand: modest

**WBL/WBR (Wing Back)** — modern wing back, used in **3-CB shapes or attack-heavy 4-back shapes**
- Bombs forward, basically **"half a W"**
- Engine demands **significantly higher** attacking skills (pace, dribbling, finishing) than LB
- Leaves big space behind; **a CB has to cover, or the center back must be good enough on the ball to step up**

**Full 10-skill comparison**:
| Skill | Fullback (LB/RB) | Wing Back (WBL/WBR) | Who's higher |
|---|---|---|---|
| **pace** | Medium | **High** | Wing back |
| **strength** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **finishing** | Low | Medium | Wing back |
| **passing** | High | High | Same |
| **dribbling** | Medium | **High** | Wing back |
| **defending** | **High** | Medium | **Fullback** |
| **positioning** | **High** | Medium | **Fullback** |
| **composure** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **freeKicks** | - | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | - | Position-independent |

**Pattern**:
- **3 skills higher for WBL** (pace/dribbling/finishing) — attacking axis, WBL needs W-level body
- **2 skills higher for LB** (defending/positioning) — defensive axis, WBL spends more on attack
- **3 skills same** (passing/strength/composure) — common base for both side roles
- **2 skills position-independent** (freeKicks/penalties) — set-piece taker quality is personal

**Key insight**: WBL is **not an upgraded LB**, it's a **role swap** — you trade defensive skills for attacking skills. defending/positioning being a bit lower is fine because the CB covers, **but they can't be too low** or WBL will be stranded in no-man's-land when they need to track back — the most common way a WBL dies.

**Practical tip**:
- 4-back traditional shape (442/433/451) → LB/RB
- 3-CB / 352 / 3412 / 343-class shapes that need wide attacking → WBL/WBR
- Signing a WBL: not just the attacking trio (pace/dribbling/finishing), **defending/positioning also need a base level** or they "go up but never come back"

> `LWB`/`RWB` is the modern 1-slot alias for WBL/WBR, same meaning in the engine.

questions: CD CDL CDR vs CB difference
is CD the same as CB
are old CD position players still in use
entries.answer:
**No difference**. `CD`/`CDL`/`CDR` is the historical name, `CB`/`CBL`/`CBR` is the current name.

The engine folds them all into the `CB` family:
- `CD` → `CB`
- `CDL` → `CB`
- `CDR` → `CB`

So:
- **Older player rows** in the database may still have `position = 'CD'`; they render and score as `CB`
- The **formation editor only accepts** `CB`/`CBL`/`CBR`
- Historical tactics rows / old data may still emit `CD*`; engine auto-compat

> This is a **pure naming cleanup** — `CD` = Centre Defender (British), `CB` = Center Back (modern global). GoalXI rolled the rename forward in 2026; old data keeps compat.

If you see a `CD` label in the UI, it's old data — treat it as `CB`.

questions: is CAM the same as CM
entries.answer:
**CM (Central Midfielder)** — midfield balance point
- Both ends of the pitch, primary job is **circulation + cover**
- Engine looks for a balance of passing, defending, and dribbling

**AM (Attacking Midfielder)** — forward-line creator
- Primary job is **final ball + chance creation**; can shoot but it's not the main role
- Engine focuses on **passing + dribbling**; defending demand is **extremely low** (AMs barely defend)

**Full 10-skill comparison**:
| Skill | Central Midfielder CM | Attacking Midfielder AM | Who's higher |
|---|---|---|---|
| **pace** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **strength** | Medium | Lower | CM |
| **finishing** | Lower | Medium | **AM** |
| **passing** | **High** | **High** | Same (both live on passing) |
| **dribbling** | Medium | **High** | **AM** |
| **defending** | Medium | **Very low** | **CM** (AM barely defends) |
| **positioning** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **composure** | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **freeKicks** | - | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | - | Position-independent |

**Pattern**:
- **3 skills higher for AM** (finishing/dribbling, + passing tied at high) — AM is attack-creator
- **2 skills higher for CM** (defending/strength) — CM is midfield shield, both attack and defend
- **4 skills same** (pace/passing/positioning/composure) — common midfielder base
- **2 skills position-independent** (freeKicks/penalties)

**One-liner**: **AM is "half a W" (barely defends), CM is "all-round midfielder" (both ends)**. AM goes up and doesn't come back; CM goes up and comes back.

**Practical tip**:
- 4-3-3 / 4-2-3-1 (double DM + 1 AM) / 4-4-2-style balanced shapes → CM
- 4-2-3-1 single AM / 4-1-2-1-2 diamond / 3-4-1-2 attack shapes → AM
- AM cannot defend; **a DM must shield behind**

> `CAM` is the historical name; engine folds to `AM`.

questions: why does DM sit behind the midfield
entries.answer:
**No functional difference**. `CDM` is the historical name for `DM`.

The engine folds them all into the `DM` family:
- `CDM` → `DM`
- `DMF` → `DM`
- `DMFL` → `DML`
- `DMFR` → `DMR`

So `CDM` = `DM` = Defensive Midfielder.

**Full 10-skill breakdown for DM**:
| Skill | DM importance | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **pace** | Medium | Need speed to track back, not the headline |
| **strength** | **High** | Physical duels and screening are DM basics |
| **finishing** | **Very low** | Almost never attacks, no requirement |
| **passing** | **High** | Intercept → distribute is DM's second core |
| **dribbling** | Medium | Occasionally carries the ball through midfield |
| **defending** | **Very high** | Headline skill, intercept + tackle first line |
| **positioning** | **Very high** | Shape the back line, tied with defending as headline |
| **composure** | Medium | Calm under pressure, no panic |
| **freeKicks** | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | Position-independent |

**Pattern**:
- **2 skills very high**: defending / positioning — DM's headline duo
- **2 skills high**: strength / passing — DM's second tier
- **3 skills medium**: pace / dribbling / composure — common midfielder base
- **1 skill very low**: finishing — almost never attacks
- **2 skills position-independent**: freeKicks / penalties

**DM's role**: last line in front of the center backs. **Intercept + circulate** is the core; create and finish are not DM's job.

**Practical tip**:
- **Single DM** (alone in the pivot): must be ball-playing (passing is enough; **defending + positioning both need to be very strong**)
- **Double pivot**: pair one pure defensive DM + one CM, complementary
- If you play an AM in front → DM is mandatory behind (AM barely defends)

questions: left center forward vs right center forward
entries.answer:
**CF (Center Forward)** — the lone 9 in a single-striker shape
- Central, primary job is scoring

**CFL (Center Forward Left)** / **CFR (Center Forward Right)**
- Used in 3-striker shapes (e.g. **3-4-3**)
- Same role as CF, just biased left / right, with more link-up play on the corresponding flank
- CFL operates mostly in the left half; CFR mostly in the right half

**Full 10-skill breakdown for CF / CFL / CFR** (base is the same; only the active zone differs):
| Skill | CF | CFL | CFR | Who's higher |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **pace** | **High** | **High** | **High** | Same |
| **strength** | **High** | **High** | **High** | Same |
| **finishing** | **Very high** | **Very high** | **Very high** | Same (all are finishers) |
| **passing** | Lower | Medium | Medium | CFL/CFR slightly higher (flank link-up) |
| **dribbling** | Medium | Medium | Medium | Same |
| **defending** | Very low | Very low | Very low | Same (forwards barely defend) |
| **positioning** | **Very high** | **Very high** | **Very high** | Same (tapping runs are core) |
| **composure** | **High** | **High** | **High** | Same (1v1 finishing) |
| **freeKicks** | - | - | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | - | - | Position-independent |

**Pattern**:
- **5 skills at very high / high (headline)**: finishing / positioning / pace / strength / composure — CF's core 5
- **1 skill medium**: dribbling — occasionally, not headline
- **1 skill lower (CF) / medium (CFL/CFR)**: passing — CF barely distributes; CFL/CFR link up with the flank
- **1 skill very low**: defending — forwards barely defend
- **2 skills position-independent**: freeKicks / penalties

**Differences between the three**:
- **CF**: central, pure finisher
- **CFL**: center-left, links with LW, slightly better passing
- **CFR**: center-right, links with RW, slightly better passing

**Practical tip**:
- Single striker (4-3-3 / 4-4-2 strike pair) → CF
- 3-striker (3-4-3) → CFL + CF + CFR trio
- Strike pair (4-4-2 / 4-1-2-1-2 diamond top) → CF + CF (two CFs, no L/R) or CF + AM

> `ST` (Striker) is an alias for `CF`, same in the engine.
> Note: `CFL`/`CFR` are **not** LW/RW — wingers are their own W family.

W player (`LW`/`RW`) full 10-skill breakdown, by on-pitch impact:

**Critical 2** (decide if a W is usable)
1. **pace** — the winger's lifeline. Counters, getting in behind, recovery runs all need speed
2. **dribbling** — 1v1 take-on, going wide / cutting inside. A W who can't dribble is useless

**Important 2** (tied)
3. **passing** — cross quality, linking with the fullback / striker
3. **finishing** — cutting inside to shoot, tap-ins

**Support 1**
5. **strength** — physical duels, holding off the opposing fullback

**Almost no impact 5**
6. **defending** — W barely defends (only emergency recovery)
7. **positioning** — W's movement is driven by dribbling, positioning matters less
8. **composure** — W rarely finishes 1v1 (crosses or cuts inside for teammates)
9. **freeKicks** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal
10. **penalties** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal

**Practical tip**:
- Signing: **pace and dribbling are the bar**; other skills can be lower
- Training: +1 pace or +1 dribbling is worth more than +1 anything else
- Rule of thumb: if a W's dribbling is clearly below average, they're effectively useless
- Don't bother chasing defending/positioning/composure — they barely register for a W

questions: what should a center back train
what skills matter for center backs
entries.answer:
CB player (`CB`/`CBL`/`CBR`) full 10-skill breakdown, by on-pitch impact:

**Critical 1**
1. **defending** — tackles, blocks, interceptions, aerial duels. The single most important CB stat

**Important 3**
2. **passing** — build-out from the back. **Modern CBs need to play out from the back**, this is heavily weighted
3. **positioning** — reading the game, covering, shifting across
4. **strength** — physical duels, headers, holding off the opposing CF

**Support 1**
5. **pace** — recovery against counters; modern CB requirements keep climbing

**Almost no impact 5**
6. **dribbling** — CBs rarely carry the ball past midfield, not headline
7. **finishing** — CBs barely join the attack for finishes
8. **composure** — CBs rarely face 1v1 with the keeper, composure barely registers
9. **freeKicks** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal
10. **penalties** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal

**Practical tip**:
- Signing: defending must be there; strength holds up aerially; positioning shouldn't be low
- Training: +1 defending is the best stat to raise
- **Don't neglect passing on a modern CB** — high press will expose a CB who can't play out
- Don't bother chasing finishing/dribbling — they barely register for a CB

questions: central midfielder defensive midfielder attacking midfielder
entries.answer:
All three midfield positions, full 10-skill breakdown, by on-pitch impact (high → low):

---

**CM (Central Midfielder)**: passing + defense, balanced
- **Headline**: **passing** (circulation) + **defending** (cover)
- **Secondary**: **dribbling** (progression, beating the press) + **positioning** (shape)
- **Support**: **composure** (calm under pressure) + **strength** (duels) + **pace** (medium)
- **Almost no impact**: **finishing** (occasional late runs, not headline) + **freeKicks/penalties** (position-independent)

---

**DM (Defensive Midfielder)**: defense + passing
- **Headline**: **defending** (tackles, interceptions, first line in front of the defense) + **positioning** (shape, screening)
- **Secondary**: **passing** (distribution, defense-to-attack) + **strength** (physical duels)
- **Support**: **composure** (calm) + **pace** (medium) + **dribbling** (medium)
- **Almost no impact**: **finishing** (almost never attacks) + **freeKicks/penalties** (position-independent)

---

**AM (Attacking Midfielder)**: dribbling + final pass
- **Headline**: **passing** (through balls, final pass) + **dribbling** (beating markers, creating)
- **Secondary**: **finishing** (arriving late to score) + **pace** (progression)
- **Support**: **composure** (medium) + **positioning** (medium) + **strength** (lower)
- **Almost no impact**: **defending** (AM barely defends) + **freeKicks/penalties** (position-independent)

---

**Three-position side-by-side comparison**:
| Skill | CM | DM | AM | Key difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **pace** | Medium | Medium | Medium | All similar |
| **strength** | Medium | Medium | Lower | AM is lighter, DM/CM hold up better |
| **finishing** | Lower | **Very low** | Medium | AM > CM > DM |
| **passing** | **High** | Medium | **High** | CM/AM feed the team, DM less so |
| **dribbling** | Medium | Medium | **High** | AM headline, CM/DM average |
| **defending** | Medium | **High** | **Very low** | DM headline, AM barely defends |
| **positioning** | Medium | **High** | Medium | DM headline (shape the back line) |
| **composure** | Medium | Medium | Medium | All similar |
| **freeKicks** | - | - | - | Position-independent |
| **penalties** | - | - | - | Position-independent |

**Core differences**:
- **CM headline**: passing + defending — all-round midfielder
- **DM headline**: defending + positioning — shield type
- **AM headline**: passing + dribbling — creator type

**Practical tip**:
- Signing CM: high passing, decent defending, decent dribbling
- Signing DM: **defending must be strong**, positioning must be there, passing enough to build (single pivot demands more)
- Signing AM: **dribbling and passing must both be strong**, with some finishing
- Training: CM/AM → dribbling + passing first; DM → defending first

questions: what should a center forward train
entries.answer:
CF player (`CF`/`CFL`/`CFR`/`ST`) full 10-skill breakdown, by on-pitch impact:

**Critical 1**
1. **finishing** — goalscoring. The CF's reason to exist. No finishing = no goals

**Important 3**
2. **positioning** — runs, tap-ins, beating the offside trap. Off-the-ball movement decides if a CF even gets the ball
3. **strength** — hold-up play, headers, wrestling with CBs
4. **composure** — calm 1-on-1s with the keeper, don't panic and sky it

**Support 2** (tied)
5. **pace** — counter runs, getting in behind
5. **dribbling** — beating the defender before shooting

**Almost no impact 4**
7. **passing** — CF distribution is weak; let the AM create, CF just finishes
8. **defending** — forwards barely defend
9. **freeKicks** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal
10. **penalties** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal

**Practical tip**:
- Signing: **finishing is the bar**
- Training: +1 finishing is the single best stat to raise
- Rule of thumb: if a CF's finishing is clearly below average, they're effectively useless (saved by keeper + skied shots)
- **Note**: CF distribution is **weak** — let the AM create, CF just finishes
- Don't bother chasing passing/defending — they barely register for a CF

GK player full 9-skill breakdown, by on-pitch impact:

**Critical 2** (decide if a GK is usable)
1. **reflexes** — save reaction. The single most important GK stat; close-range shots saved or not
2. **handling** — catching cleanly. High balls claimed, low shots held not parried

**Important 1**
3. **positioning** — shape, narrowing angles, being in the right place reduces the save difficulty

**Support 2** (tied)
4. **aerial** — high-ball claiming
4. **composure** — calm, no fumbles

**Almost no impact 4**
6. **pace** — GK doesn't need to chase balls past midfield, barely registers
7. **strength** — GK doesn't need to wrestle strikers, barely registers
8. **freeKicks** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal
9. **penalties** — position-independent, set-piece taker quality is personal

**Comparison vs outfield players**:
- GK **ignores pace/strength** (those fields exist but don't enter GK save rating)
- GK cares about the 3 GK-specific technical skills (reflexes/handling/aerial) + positioning + composure
- A high reflexes/handling radar means a good GK; **pace/strength on a GK are basically irrelevant** — don't read a high radar and assume a good GK

**Practical tip**:
- Signing: reflexes and handling are the bar
- Training: +1 reflexes is the most valuable; +1 handling second
- Rule of thumb: a GK with reflexes clearly below average will be beaten constantly; handling clearly below average will fumble high balls
- Don't bother chasing pace/strength — they barely register for a GK

questions: difference between GOLD SILVER BRONZE tier
entries.answer:
**Specialties** = the player's "identity tag", an engine multiplier on specific match events.

**12 active specialties** (each has an engine hook):
| Specialty | Best for position | Triggered event |
|---|---|---|
| AERIAL_THREAT | CB/CF | Headers, aerial duels |
| DRIBBLER | W/AM | 1v1 take-on |
| PLAYMAKER | AM/CM | Through balls, final pass |
| TACKLER | CB/DM | Tackles, interceptions |
| WALL | CB/DM | Defensive blocks |
| SPEEDSTER | W | Counter runs |
| CROSSER | W/LB | Wide crosses |
| POACHER | CF | Tap-ins, rebounds |
| COMPOSED | CF/AM | One-on-one finishing |
| PHYSICAL_BEAST | CB/CF | Physical duels |
| SAVING_MASTER | GK | Key saves |
| SWEEPER_KEEPER | GK | Sweeping / rushing out |

**Tier**:
- **GOLD** — top tier, largest engine bonus when triggered
- **SILVER** — mid tier, medium bonus
- **BRONZE** — basic tier, smallest bonus

**Key points**:
- Only **~50%** of players have a specialty (the other half have none)
- Tier is **independent of player attributes** — it's rolled at generation time, not derived
- **Per event, only the team's strongest specialty is applied**, no stacking. So multiple POACHERs in one team only count the strongest one
- Specialties show up in the transfer market filters and scout reports

> Legacy v1 specialties (HEADER/LPASS/...) are deprecated; new-gen players don't roll them.

questions: how do player stamina form injury affect matches
entries.answer:
Three different concepts, each affects matches differently:

---

**stamina** — the player's **current-match** fitness
- Drains continuously during a match (running, duels, saves all cost)
- Affects **this match's** contribution (low stamina = below-par performance)
- Recovers via substitutions and halftime rest
- Shown as the fitness bar on the player card during a match

---

**form** — the player's **recent** competitive state
- Affects PWI display (good form → PWI reads slightly higher; bad form → slightly lower)
- Drifts based on recent match results and training
- Shown as the form arrow (↑/→/↓) on the radar / card

---

**injury** — the player's **current** injury state
- `severe` (out — can't play) / `minor` (playable but reduced) / `null` (healthy)
- Type: muscle / ligament / joint / head / other
- Severity drives recovery time (minor = days, severe = weeks)
- New injuries can trigger from in-match events (tackles, overuse, etc.)

---

**How they relate**:
- `stamina` is **in-match**, `form` is **between matches**, `injury` is **a state machine**
- Player enters injury list → countdown to recovery → state clears to play again

> Cumulative match minutes also influences form drift; long stretches without playing → form drops.

questions: how to list a player for sale
how to set startPrice and buyout
entries.answer:
Two different operations, completely separate flows:

---

**Release**
- Soft delete, **youth players only**
- `POST /players/:id/release`; the player row is **kept** (event history is preserved), but `deletedAt` is filled in
- **Senior players cannot be released** (the API returns an error) — by design, prevents a UI typo from dumping a first-team starter
- To clear a senior from the squad, use List-for-sale or wait out the contract

---

**List Player**
- `POST /transfers/auctions` (in the squad page, click a player → "List Player" button)
- Fields required:
  - **startPrice** — the lowest sale price you'll accept (€)
  - **buyout** — hidden field; **currently auto = startPrice × 2** (the v2 mechanic isn't exposed to players yet)
- After listing, the player's `onTransfer = true`; other teams can bid
- The auction is public in the transfer market (other team AIs will bid)
- Sold → player transfers to the buyer team, you get the money
- Unsold (no bid) → re-list or delist

---

**Web flow**:
```
Team → Squad → pick player → "List Player" → fill startPrice → submit
```

**Practical tip**:
- startPrice: low if you want a quick sale, high if you're waiting for a big fish (could be a long wait)
- Release: only for **youth players you don't want** or **youth-development failures**; never release a senior
- Auction timeline: 1-2 game days with no bids after listing is normal

questions: what types of events are in player history
what does TRANSFER HAT_TRICK INJURY mean
full list of player achievement events
how many event types exist on a player timeline
entries.answer:
The player detail page's "event history" area has **14 event types**, grouped into 4 categories:

---

**Transfer / contract (2)**
| Event | Trigger | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **TRANSFER** | Player moves to another team (buy / sell / free) | Permanent transfer record |
| **CONTRACT_RENEWAL** | Player extends contract with the team | Contract extended |

---

**Achievement (5)**
| Event | Trigger | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **CHAMPIONSHIP_TITLE** | The player's team wins the league | Historic team moment |
| **GOLDEN_BOOT** | Top scorer of the season | Top-tier finisher badge |
| **ASSISTS_LEADER** | Top assist maker of the season | Top-tier creator badge |
| **TACKLES_LEADER** | Top tackler of the season | Top-tier defender badge |
| **MAN_OF_THE_MATCH** | Best player in a single match | Single-match award |

---

**Career milestone (4)**
| Event | Trigger | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **DEBUT** | First appearance for the team (any competition) | Career first match |
| **LEAGUE_DEBUT** | First league appearance for the team | League first match (recorded separately) |
| **CAPTAIN_DEBUT** | First match as captain | First game wearing the armband |
| **RECORD_BROKEN** | Breaks a club or league record | History-making moment |

---

**Special (3)**
| Event | Trigger | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **HAT_TRICK** | 3+ goals in a single match | Hat trick |
| **YOUTH_PROMOTION** | Youth player promoted to senior squad | Promoted from youth to first team (ties into the youth module) |
| **INJURY** | Player gets injured | Injury record (pair with the condition-form-injury entry) |

---

**How to read event history**:
- The player detail page has an **Events** tab / timeline area
- Listed in **reverse chronological order** (newest at the top)
- Each event shows: **event type + date + short description** (e.g. `HAT_TRICK · 2026-08-15 · 3 goals`)
- Different events have different color icons: **gold = achievement** (CHAMPIONSHIP_TITLE / GOLDEN_BOOT / HAT_TRICK), **red = injury** (INJURY), **green = promotion** (YOUTH_PROMOTION), **blue = transfer / contract** (TRANSFER / CONTRACT_RENEWAL), **purple = milestone** (RECORD_BROKEN / DEBUT etc.)

---

**Practical use — how event history tells you a player's value**:
- **Quality**: density of **gold achievements** (HAT_TRICK / CHAMPIONSHIP_TITLE / RECORD_BROKEN / GOLDEN_BOOT) — more = worth more
- **Durability**: frequency of **INJURY** — frequent = injury-prone, sign with caution
- **Loyalty**: count of **CONTRACT_RENEWAL** — many = core / senior player
- **Path**: **DEBUT** + **YOUTH_PROMOTION** dates — youth promotion = homegrown, usually higher PWI ceiling
- **Big-game ability**: frequency of **MAN_OF_THE_MATCH** — high = clutch player

> These are all 14 types shown in the player detail page's "event history" area. Click a player → detail page → Events tab for the full timeline.

questions: why are veterans better at penalties
do national team games grow experience faster
entries.answer:
**Experience (EXP)** = a player's **long-term accumulated match value**, the long-term counterpart of `form` (short-term). **Higher number = more "seasoned" the player is**.

---

**Basic rules**:
- After every match, players who appeared get experience based on their performance
- Experience **only goes up** — injury / bad form / rest don't drain it
- Experience is **automatically converted to a level (1-20)**; higher level means stronger **veteran bonus** (especially on penalties)
- Max level is 20; once full, extra exp overflows without further level-up

---

**How experience grows (per match type)**:

| Match type | EXP multiplier | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **National team** | **5.0x** | **Fastest growth** — one match = 5 league matches of exp |
| **Playoff** | 2.0x | 2× league |
| **League / Cup** | 1.0x (baseline) | Standard |
| **Friendly** | **0.1x** | Almost no growth |
| **Tournament** | 0 | No exp credited |

**Minutes played also matter**: **play 90 minutes = full base exp for that match**; play 45 minutes = half; sub on for 10 minutes = almost nothing.

---

**The "veteran bonus" by level**:
- Engine uses experience in `calculatePenaltyMultiplier` and `getMultiplierWithFitnessFactor`
- **Engine comment**: `"Penalty specific multiplier: Ignores stamina, high experience bonus."` — **veterans are more reliable on penalties**, not affected by fatigue
- Long-term play: high-experience players are more consistent (similar to form but for the long haul)
- Short-term play is still form-driven; experience is the **long-term trend**

---

**How to see experience**:
- The player detail page / player card / squad page board all show an **EXP** badge with the **raw number**
- The level (1-20) is **not separately shown to players**, but the engine uses it to compute bonuses
- The radar / skill panel **does not** show experience (exp is meta-data, not an on-pitch skill)

---

**Practical tips**:
- Want to grow exp fast → **play your players in national team matches** (5x rate)
- Friendly and tournament matches are basically "free play" (almost no exp), but useful for tuning form and testing lineups
- Young players with low PWI shouldn't be sold just for that — **exp keeps growing**, and a high-exp veteran with a slightly lower PWI still has the veteran bonus
- Veterans (high exp) take **penalties far more reliably** than youngsters — pick the experienced player for the decisive spot kick
- Higher levels cost more exp to reach (the upgrade cost grows fast in the later levels); you need **long-term playing time + high-quality matches** to climb

> Note: experience **only grows from matches**, not from training. Youth players promoted with little playing time will have low experience.

---

**Relationship to other concepts**:
- vs **form**: form is **short-term state** (1-2 week drift), experience is **long-term accumulation**. Both affect PWI display, but **long-term performance** leans on experience, **single-match performance** leans on form
- vs **PWI**: PWI is the **composite rating** = current skills + experience + form, all factored in. Experience is one **input factor** (multiplier)
- vs **currentSkills**: skills are **ability**, experience is **seasoning**. High skills + low exp = talented but raw; average skills + max exp = stable but capped
